correctness.rationale: Direct distance stratification: every non-leaf nilpotent is a hub-crossing singleton arrow (2m cases, rank1/index2) or a distinct-leaf hub path (m(m-1) cases, rank2/index3). Nilpotent leaf restrictions are labeled unordered sets of oriented paths, with exponential generating function exp(sum_{j<=L} x^j u^(j-1)). A conditioned independent Poisson assembly with means rho^j, rho/(1-rho)^2=m, gives the maximum-path extreme. Tail expected weight O(sqrt(m)log m) and variance O(m log^2 m) vanish relative to full Gaussian conditioning scale m^(3/4), while the no-large-component intensity tends to e^(-s), giving Gumbel. Direct enumeration m=1..6 matched all rank/index fibres; numerical coefficient tests m=100,500,2000 check convergence direction.
